 Federal authorities previously searched the former congressman's DC home and seized his electronic devices in August
 By
 Anders Hagstrom , Louis Casiano Fox News 
 Published

 close Video FBI raids Beverly Hills mansion as part of Eric Swalwell investigation 
 Federal authorities raided a California mansion related to an investigation into former Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., on Tuesday morning.
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 BEVERLY HILLS – Federal authorities raided a California mansion related to an investigation into disgraced former Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., on Tuesday morning, Fox News has learned.
 Swalwell resigned from Congress and withdrew from the California gubernatorial race earlier this year after facing multiple accusations of sexual misconduct. The FBI's raid targeted a mansion in Beverly Hills.
 In August, the FBI searched Swalwell's D.C. home and seized his electronic devices at San Francisco International Airport during an operation. The operation was related to a probe into sexual misconduct, according to sources familiar with the incident. He was not arrested or detained.
 FBI SEIZES SWALWELL’S DEVICES AT AIRPORT AS SEXUAL MISCONDUCT INVESTIGATION ESCALATES: SOURCES 
 Rep. Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.) speaks during a House Judiciary Committee hearing with FBI Director Kash Patel in the Rayburn House Office Building on Sept. 17, 2025. (Win McNamee/Getty Images) 
 At least five women, including one former staffer, have accused Swalwell of sexual misconduct or rape.
 Swalwell also faced renewed scrutiny earlier this week after the White House declassified documents related to an FBI probe into his relationship with Christine "Fang Fang" Fang , a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Swalwell told FBI agents he had "physical relations" with Fang on a handful of occasions, according to declassified FBI records released Monday by the White House.
 Their last sexual encounter occurred in March 2015, according to Swalwell’s account in the FBI records.
 The documents were released by the White House's new Government Transparency Task Force.
 SWALWELL OUT AMID SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS AFTER 13 YEARS IN CONGRESS 
 Federal authorities raided a California mansion related to an investigation into disgraced former Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., on Tuesday morning, Fox News has learned. (Fox News Digital/Louis Casiano) 
 Swalwell was interviewed by the FBI first in May 2015 and later in March 2016 regarding his relationship with Fang.
 Fang had suspected ties to China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS), and her parents were reportedly considered known Chinese intelligence officers.
 SWALWELL CALLS SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS 'FLAT OUT FALSE,' SAYS HE WILL FIGHT THEM 'WITH EVERYTHING' 
 Lonna Drewes, a woman with sexual misconduct allegations against U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell, reacts as she holds a press conference with her attorneys Lisa Bloom and Arick Fudali in Beverly Hills, California, on April 14, 2026. (Jill Connelly/Reuters) 
 CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP 
 The former lawmaker left office in April after being threatened with expulsion from the House before his exit. He spent 13 years as a member of Congress.
 "I will fight the serious false allegations made against me," Swalwell wrote at the time of his resignation. "However, I must take responsibility and ownership for the mistakes I did make."
 Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.
